t: Speak with Dobrinya Bykov in the Main Square to learn more about becoming a warrior.

Hear ye! Hear ye!
Can you hold a weapon? Do you believe in freedom, equality, and brotherhood? Then our trainers of Novograd are here to set you on the path to victory!
Our wisest and most experienced trainers are eager to share their knowledge with you!
Oho, you're interested in becoming a warrior? How commendable! As a warrior, you'll master the art of close combat. How exciting!
Let me just check my list... Ah, Dobrinya Bykov! He will be your trainer. Don't just stand around, you need to go make yourself useful to the League!
Hm, you wish to become a warrior? Stand up straight, child! You need to have discipline if you wish to learn from me!
Gather 3 Lynx Fangs and Lynx Claws and bring them to the Bugeyed Family in the Scout Camp.

We were well known hunters on Isa. We used to spend our days helping them on their hunts. One of their experienced hunters would often say - "like cures like." We took it to mean that the thing that kills you can also cure you.
Northwest of here is the Twilight Forest where the lynx live. One of the beasts wounded a fella of ours already - we're going to have to face them more than once if we want to survive here.
That's why we're going to make weapons! But first, we'll need to gather sharp tips for them. Lynx fangs and claws will do just fine for that purpose. Get them for us and we'll give you the first weapon we make.
Great! Sharp and strong claws and fangs - all you need to make good hunting weapons!
Kill 3 Ginger Lynxes, then find and kill the Great Ginger Lynx in the Twilight Forest. Report to Nikolai Rubtsov in the Scout Camp.

There's nothing worse than being a burden on others. Damn! If not for these wounds I would go out there and slay the menace myself...
You see, we were attacked while scouting. Several beasts ambushed us from the thicket - I fought like a mad Orc! I was pushing my way through, cat after cat - but there was one special lynx among them, a strong and massive beast.
Look! These scars on my chest are her signature. An underhanded strike! She attacked me and used the cover of her fellow lynx to escape!
Take vengeance for me. Go into the Twilight Forest and kill ten of those ginger beasts. Then find the great lynx in the eastern part of the forest and kill that ugly thing.
I'll have a good reward waiting for you.
Have I been avenged? Are those ginger rogues dead?
Great job! I only wish I could have done it myself. Please choose your reward.
Gather 5 Plantain Leaves and take them to Alfred de Delice at the Scout Camp.

The recent accident has shown that we are unprepared for life on this allod. If not for the plantain shrub that happened to be nearby, the man would have bled to death.

Unfortunately, this is the only medicinal herb we have found here. It grows all over the allod, but this place is rather dangerous.

Could you please bring me five plantain leaves? I've run out, and we'd do well to have some of it in reserve.
Have you found any plantain leaves?

Good. Now we're prepared for any surprises.
If you manage to find more, we would be grateful!
Find Mila Dubovskaya and Veleslav Seversky in the Twilight Forest. Defeat Veleslav, recover the Chest of Meteorite Stones and return it to Amanda.

I have a bit of a problem at the moment. You see, Mila Dubovskaya and Veleslav Seversky went out scouting with us. They're both from noble society, very respected in Kania. They were quarrelling quite loudly and I heard Veleslav was saying something about his brother, that he fights for truth.
I didn't pay attention to the details. Those are human issues and Elves aren't interested in petty quarrels. But maybe I was wrong to ignore them this time.
They were supposed to come back several hours ago, but no one has seen them. I'm worried something might have happened.
To make matters worse, Mila asked me to give her several of those Stones from my Uncle's lab. I saw no harm in letting her study them, but I would like them back eventually! Search for them in the Twilight Forest, find them, and recover the chest full of Meteorite Stones.
Ah, so you're back. What happened?

What a scoundrel! All of that fuss over nobility and honor. I will never understand how humans can be so silly. Now beauty... that's something worth quarreling over. Anyway, thank you for saving Mila and returning this chest to me.
Accompany Mila back to the camp and notify Amanda de Desirae.

Thank the Light! I owe you. Veleslav... Oh, I'm so ashamed to speak about that. You see, Seversky is an ancient and respected family, relatives of the Valirs! But they are also the ones responsible for our troubles.
You see, him and his brother Boris helped get the rebels in to Clement's Tower. Their goal was to steal this strange chest of meteorite stones and any other useful materials to aid them in a rebellion against the Kanian government!
Amanda managed to get the stones first, so Veleslav decided to pose as a refugee in hopes of stealing them from her later. He didn't want to draw attention to himself, so he blackmailed me into getting them from Amanda myself. Turns out he was planning on killing me anyway once I finished his task. Only you saved me from death!
Please help me get back to the Scout Camp. And tell Amanda about what happened... I'll be too embarrassed to show my face to her for a long time.
Have you found Mila and Veleslav?
What?! Veleslav was partially responsible for my uncle's death? Kanian noblemen! They are a disgrace to the League! And now my uncle is dead because of these horrible stones...
Use the Scroll of Healing on Ton the Windblower and talk to Daniel de Pluie.

While you were gone, some very interesting developments came to light. The scouts found a Gibberling that had been badly wounded on the northern coast. He must thank Tensess for our appearing here! He's at death's door with terrible wounds inflicted on him by some unknown monster.
Luckily, there was a Scroll of Healing in the box of supplies. I'd very much like to have a chat with him. If he's been here for a long time, he might be able to shed some light on a few of this allod's mysteries.
You'll find him by the hut on the northern coast. Use the scroll and ask him any questions you can. If there are any problems, talk to Daniel. He's there doing all he can to save the poor Gibberling.
Poor thing... I wonder who would want to hurt this Gibberling?

The Gibberling is safe for now. His wounds have been healed and death no longer threatens him. But this mysterious native is clearly out of his mind. His eyes are hazy and he cannot speak in coherent sentences. The sad condition he's in was apparently caused by something more than just physical injuries.
Bring 3 pieces of Stringy Crab Meat to Daniel de Pluie.

Perhaps the cause of his insanity is simple. Hunger! Look at how emaciated he is!

Now, there are many crabs in this area. And the heaps of shells around the patient's hut indicate that to have been his staple diet. Perhaps the injuries have made him unable to gain sustenance, which led to hunger and, in turn, madness. This can be verified easily as well as fixed if the hypothesis is correct.

Bring me three pieces of crab meat. We'll feed the patient and check this first theory.
Have you brought the crab meat?
Look! He's definitely showing some signs of recovery. At the very least he understands that this is food and what to do with it. What an appetite!
Collect a Giant Crab Head from the Giant Thorny Crab and bring it to Daniel de Pluie.

The last of my theories pertains to the terrible wounds suffered by our patient. Judging by the bite marks, it was definitely not a lynx.
Perhaps the cause of his madness is fear. Something scared him immensely and the Gibberling went insane. Dilated pupils and that indistinct babble are the first symptoms of such madness.
Shock therapy is the only cure in cases such as this. The patient experiences a shock so great that the new fear overcomes the previous one, bringing him back to his right mind.
I've seen some prints left by a giant crab's nippers on the coast. These creatures aren't normally beautiful and if it is an especially gigantic and ugly one...
Hey, that's an idea. The tracks lead eastwards along the coast. Go find this grotesque beast, kill it, and bring me its head. We'll show it to our patient and... well, we'll see what happens.
Did you manage to find the giant crab?

Oh, Great Astral! It's a monster! If this doesn't work, I don't know what else we could even attempt to try.
Let's show this loathsome thing to our patient... Aha! It's working! Our Gibberling is definitely regaining his senses...
Find the Gibberling Family Portrait and bring it to Daniel de Pluie.

Another theory concerning the cause of his insanity is loneliness. He has apparently been living on the allod alone for the past few years. No wonder he has lost his wits!
To bring him back to normal, we'll need something from his past, some kind of memoir from his previous life. Our patient's hut is made of the remains of an Astral ship, we can assume he wrecked on some nearby rocks.
Search the coast for the crash site. Perhaps you will find something that can remind the Gibberling of his past and restore his sanity.

Wow, his family's portrait! If loneliness is the cause of his madness, this is the best possible cure!
...Look! He's crying! This means he's regaining his... um... Gibberling feelings!
Relay Ton the Windblower's story to Amanda de Desirae at the Scout Camp.

Now I can rest easy. It's time to tell you what happened just recently.

The last thing I remember is our encounter with some strange Kanians. I was so happy when I heard the voices! But those evil people just laughed at me. They sicced a giant bear on me!

So that's what you should know: there's some good power dwelling here. But there are also malicious people...

We need to find a way out of here... or else this island will become our grave! Tell that to everyone in your camp so you don't make the same mistakes...
What have you learned from the Gibberling?
Well, well. Now it's all starting to add up. I'll have a new mission for you.
Find a Ghostly Light and place it near the June Ruins on the northwest shore. Report back to Alfred de Delice

Now that we have what we need, let's think of how to get off this allod. Amanda thinks the chances of survival are pretty small, and there's little hope of outside help - as huge as the Astral is, the odds of a ship passing by are slim to none. But me, I believe in the best!
Lok told me that the western shore is inhabited by will-o'-the-wisps. These creatures are cryptic enough, but now's not the time to study them. We'll just go on what we know about them.
You'll have to kill them to find the ghost lights. This supernatural substance can maintain a steady radiance for a long while. Once you find one, you'll have to set it on somewhere on the shore that's elevated - the June ruin should do.
If a ship should pass by, the crew will notice our signal. This is our chance and we can't let it slip by!
Were you able to set up the signal light?
Wonderful! Now all we have to do is wait... Wait and hope!
Take the Ship's Log to Amanda de Desirae.

One of our scouts, Lok, was sent to explore the southeastern part of the allod. Can you guess what he found? An Astral ship crashed on the rocks! Lok claims that it was the same exact ship he'd seen at Clement's Tower immediately before the catastrophe.
Perhaps these ‘others' who attacked the Gibberling were on that ship. Maybe fate has thrown us together with the culprits responsible for Clement's Tower! This must be investigated. Lok says the ship is crawling with the undead and didn't dare to poke his head in, but you're tough enough to do that.
Go to the southeast shore, find the ship, and investigate. What I'm really interested in is the ship's log. Once we have it, we can decide what to do next.
Have you found the ship's log yet?

Give me a moment to look into the ship's log.
So... Hm, oh dear.
Oho! That explains a lot.
Bring 3 Owl Feathers, a Birch Bark Scroll, and Black Chokeberries to Alfred de Delice in the Scout Camp.

I miss putting a pen to paper more than anything else. I feel my duty is to chronicle our adventures. This story could become extremely popular when we return to the mainland!
And with good reason. A group of men, Elves, and Gibberlings miraculously end up on a deserted allod. A mysterious benefactor, some evil enemies, a terrible polar bear... No one has ever written anything like this!
You can help me. I've seen some black chokeberry bushes nearby, I can make ink out of those. And there have been owls spotted to the west of here, their feathers will make fine pens. Birch bark can be used as my paper.
Bring all that to me and I'll make you my book's main character. "The Mysterious Isle," I'll call it! Or even better - "Lost!" It'll be a true masterpiece!
Have you managed to find everything I need for my book?
This is perfect! Now if you will please excuse me, I've got some writing to do.
Find Lok in the cave to the northeast.

Let's see... The wrecked ship is definitely the one we saw at Clement's Tower. When my uncle died and everyone was rushing to escape, the captain realized too late that his passengers were rebels and murderers. The crew tried to arrest the criminals but failed. The captain then crashed the ship against the rocky shore. This was how they found themselves here.
I feel like the whole incident is coming to a head. While you were absent, our mysterious benefactor brought us another present. It contains weapons and a note. The letter said that the rebels from the wrecked ship have found his shelter. It's hidden in a deep cave in the Eastern part of the allod.
He asks us to help expel them, promising to send us to Kania in exchange for our help. This is our chance!
I've already sent Lok, our best scout, to search the cave but I'm sure he could use some help. Follow Lok's trail, find him, and... well, frankly, I don't know what to do next. You better play it by ear.
Oh, you've come just in time!

Oh, shame on me, shame on me! Caught like some sort of greenhorn! All because I was alone - I wish Shpok and Glok were here. Oh, man!
Well, every cloud has a silver lining, right? I managed to uncover some information and, more importantly, steal from those cutthroats. Look at these beautiful weapons I pinched! You can choose anything you like.
Kill Arsene de Vevre and talk to the Nameless One.

Okay, here's the situation. Our mysterious benefactor has been living on this allod as a hermit for many years and is apparently a very powerful mage. He's the one that's been helping the shipwrecked Gibberling, and when we appeared together with those bastard criminals that attacked our mage, he decided to do the same for both groups.
But the others have worked out where his shelter is. This is where I came into the story. One of the attackers, a necromancer, threatened to kill me if our benefactor didn't hand his ship over to them. And guess what? He agreed! I'm shocked!
The bay where his ship is docked can be accessed through this cave. Many of them have already started boarding, so you must hurry! My advice is to find the necromancer first - he stayed behind to ward off any intruders. You must deal with him and then find our benefactor's shelter.
What can I do for you?
I've seen you before... You're one of those who came through the portal. Perhaps you'll be able to achieve what I cannot.
Find an Access Crystal for The Nameless One.

Normally I hate to ask for favors since it goes against my solitary nature, but those loathsome mutineers have stolen all of the access crystals for my ship. We're going to need to find one if you want to get on board.
Go down there and slay as many as you need to. One of them must have a crystal on them.
How did it go? Did you manage to find one?
Excellent! But what I'm going to ask you to do next will be tough...
Use the boarding device to teleport to the ship, find the Ancient June Cup, Sacrificial Dagger and Obsidian Rod and bring them to the Nameless One.

This choice is completely tearing me apart! It's putting your life on the line by taking out these delinquents versus keeping my pledge.
I'm sorry, but right now the former means more to me.
We'll have to board the ship and in order to do that we'll need that crystal you plucked from a mutineer earlier.
These outlaws are led by a druid whose terrifying pet polar bear is almost always by his side, they'll be carrying a sacrificial dagger and an ancient June cup. Those two are the core of this gang and your key target. Your other target is their navigator, she'll have an obsidian rod.
With those three gone, these criminals will easily be crushed! When you're done, bring these items back to me and I will help you and your friends leave this allod.
So the menace is done with... Now it is time for you to leave my allod. First you must choose your reward.
Use the June ruins to travel to the allod where the rescue ship is set to arrive when you are ready to leave Evermeet Isle.

I've contacted a Kanian patrol ship. It will be here shortly to take you and your friends back to Kania. However, I would like to keep my part in this story secret.
That is why the ship has been ordered to dock at a small allod not far from here. This way you and your companions can be rescued without me ever being seen.
Soon I too will leave this allod - it has already become unsuitable for fulfilling my vow of solitude. One of your friends, if not you, may give away my secret and I need to find peace.
When you are ready, use the June ruins to travel to the spot the ship is set to arrive. I wish you the best of luck in your future adventures!
That sounds pretty amazing! Too bad we don't have time to stay and chat. The ship to Kania will be here any moment! Perhaps we shall meet again under happier circumstances!
Visit the Gibberling Embassy in Novograd and relate Ton the Windblower's story.

At long last I saw the mage I owe my life to! He's a strange one. I tried to thank him, and he started waving his hands and talking ‘bout some urgent business. Ah, to heck with him!
I decided to wait for the others with the Elf. Since you'll be the first to Novograd, will you do me a favor? Please visit the Gibberling Embassy in the Gibberling District and tell them my story. I'm sorry to say that my search has failed. I was not able to find the Gibberling homeland but maybe other scouts will have more luck.
Thank you for everything. Losing my sisters was a serious blow, I tell you. But I will continue on my way, perhaps together with Lok, another loner like myself. Together we'll have an easier time dealing with our loss. Maybe we'll meet again one day!
We are the Gray Family, the Gibberling Ambassadors in Novograd. Asgerd, Stein, and Torvar. It is our great pleasure to make your acquaintance. What news do you have?
I see. Even though that expedition failed, I'm sure that one will eventually find our beloved homeland.
Report to the Novograd Detective Bureau on everything that occurred on Evermeet Isle.

Our mysterious benefactor has sent Ton and I to this small allod. The others should soon be here as well. Tell me, did the mage introduce himself to you? No? I wonder who he is. What a curious man...
Don't bother waiting for the others. Take the first ship you see and head on over to the League headquarters in Novograd. Everything that happened at Clement's Tower and our experience here on this allod must be reported at once! There is a rebellion developing and it must be stopped before it's too late!
It's amazing. I was at Clement's Tower for military training to fight against the Empire. I didn't expect war to catch us so soon. And right here in the very heart of the League! We're caught in the middle of great changes, I can feel it. When you get back to Novograd make sure to report to the proper authorities immediately. I'm sure the League will want to know what happened.
Information pertaining to the rebels? We need any kind of information we can get now. Go ahead, I'm listening.
Kill the Damned Soul and notify Ton the Windblower.

Turn around, don't look... I'm crying here like a girl, but I can't help it... I remember everything now...

My name is Ton the Windblower. My sisters and I were on an important mission, but our ship hit these rocks... I was completely alone here for three years. And I would have probably died... If some mysterious benefactor hadn't provided me with supplies and weapons!

I want to ask a favor of you...

My loneliness on the island was particularly awful because sometimes I saw it... The cursed Spark. Or rather... it found me.

They say cursed Sparks are the doomed souls of evil people, orcs, elves... But I doubt even churchmen can make sense of it all. I know one thing for certain - there's ill will in this Spark! It's a vicious enemy that knows no fear or mercy!

We might be able to leave the island. But even on the mainland, the thought that it might find me again will keep me up at night. It needs to be destroyed. Do it, and I will be able to regain my peace of mind.
Sometimes I think that she wants to be destroyed so she can rest in peace. But when I tried to fight her, I nearly died myself!
Thank you. Now I can sleep peacefully.
Bring 20 average potions of Determination to the Attentive Family at the Quiet Harbor to improve your reputation with the Gibberlings.

Are you an alchemist, by any chance?

We could really use one right now! There are enemies all around - snow monsters, harpies, bears... We can hardly manage to shoot them down as they come! It's so cold that it takes half a dozen arrows to hit the target.

So if you want to earn the Gibberlings' gratitude and improve your reputation, bring us 20 average potions of Determination. That's going to be good for everyone!
Bring us anything of use, anything! Now, we especially need Potions of Determination.
Wow, thanks! On behalf of all Gibberlings, thank you!
Find the 3 Stones around Frozen Frontier and report back to the Slider Family in Quiet Harbor.

There are these funny stones all around Frozen Frontier. We're not too sure what their original purpose was, but we like to use them to figure out what island we're on since they each have different markings on them!
See, the Bold Hill stone has squiggles that look like this and the Shaggy Island squiggles are similar, but this one particular squiggle really stands out! And the squiggles on the stone on stone on Nordheim are something else completely! It's all very interesting!
You should go check it out for yourself! And then come back and tell me if you can figure out what the squiggles say.
Hurry up! I want to see if you know what they say!

You found them?
Oh, you don't know what they say either. How disappointing.
Collect 4 Frozen Frontier Trophies from the most dangerous creatures and return to the Slider Family in Quiet Harbor.

It's scary out there. It's okay to admit it. We know it!
Especially with creatures out there like Sagefeather, Bartach, Icemaw, Nightscreech, Razika, and Arkando Icefist! But work must be done! So we want you to go out there and face your fears. It's the only way we'll be able to know for sure that you're not afraid of the beasties that lurk in the dark!
Bring us back four trophies from nasty creatures like the ones that we named off and we'll make sure to tell everyone that you're the bravest adventurer we know!
Have you found and trophies yet?

See! I knew you were brave!
My brother here wasn't so sure, but you really showed him!
Kill 50 miners on the islands of Frozen Frontier and return to the Slider Family in Quiet Harbor.

This land doesn't completely belong to the Gibberlings. The mountainfolk miners have proved to be a huge threat to us and this land!
They're stealing all the natural resources! And to make matters worse, those nasty miners are completely feral! They're like wild animals out there! They just won't listen to reason...
And that's where you come in. We want you do go out there an teach them all a lesson! Let them know that if they don't want to end up on the endangered species list, they better make nice with us!
Those hooligans better fear your name now!

Thank you!
It'll be so much safer here on Frozen Frontier for us Gibberlings now!
Find and collect 5 samples of Astral Ice Essence for the Slider Family in Quiet Harbor.

Frozen Frontier makes something that everyone wants! Something that's invaluable to the League and only we have it!
We're talking about Astral ice essence, of course! It's a magical substance that can only be made when the Astral meets the extreme cold. So magical that even the great mages are drooling themselves over it! Aidenus is constantly asking about our captains if they brought the essence back to Novograd.
So we want you to go out and see if you can't find any that we can send to Aidenus!
You can find stones with Astral ice essence all along the shores of Frozen Frontier.

Amazing!
I'm sure Aidenus will start doing flips once he sees all this!
Complete all of the Slider Family's tasks and return to them in Quiet Harbor.

If you do everything that we ask, then we promise to give you one of our most prized treasures! We're sure that it will help you on any adventure that you chose to take from here on out!
So, please help us with the squiggly stones, miners, and dangerous beasties!

Thank you! You have no idea how big of a help you've been!
Go ahead and take whatever reward you'd like!
Kill an Icy Dragon on Nordheim Isle and return to the Cunning Family.

So, now we know how to fight the dragon. And more importantly, we know that we can win. It's simply a matter of knowing the correct strategy!
It's time to put an end to these monsters. Nordheim Isle is to be the new hunting ground for the Gibberlings - and for you too! For every dragon you kill we'll be eternally grateful.
Just make sure you are well-prepared. Nordheim is a tough place, the cold can freeze you out before you reach your opponents. Bring some ale and whatever useful potions you can find!
Security comes first! That's our captain's motto!
Good job! We thank you on behalf of all the Gibberlings!
Use the June ruins to get to another allod and return to the Stubborn Family.

The only way to move between the allods of this archipelago is to use the ancient teleportation trails. They're made of magical energy that goes from one June ruin to another.
At first it's a little frightening using the power of the ruins. You have to float over the Astral with nothing but a magical sphere to keep you from falling forever! We nearly passed out the first time we tried it. Unfortunately, there's no other way to move between the allods.
If you're going to be spending some time here you better get used to it. We suggest you try the ruins out as soon as possible. Come back to us when you're done and tell us what you think!
When we first decided to use the ruins, we were terribly frightened! But now we're used to it and we even like it!
Speak to the Cunning Family in Frozen Frontier.

Fortunately, we've gotten our cargo back. The thing is, our ship's still busted and we can't leave! We've run out of meteorite ore. We feel so foolish. Only a moronic Orc would run out of something like that.
Are you heading for Frozen Frontier any time soon? It's a small archipelago to the northwest of here. It's a territory that was gifted to us Gibberlings by a Kanian lord.
We know for a fact that the Little Sparrow is moored there. Her captains are old friends of ours. We know they'll find a way to get an emergency supply of meteorite to us if you could take a message to them about our troubles.

Of course we know all about the Sludge Splitter - she's an excellent vessel, especially if she's properly captained. We remember sailing side by side with the Sludge Splitter in the Astral - those show-offs overtook us and then offered to tow us!
We're not surprised that her captains ended up running into trouble. Well, we can hardly ignore the plight of our fellow Gibberlings, can we? We'll send a crate of meteorite to help those hapless fellows soon. Thanks for informing us.
Speak with Torn the Stutterer in Quiet Harbor.

Well, hello... hic. Sorry... there's nothing left. There's nothing worse for a Gibberling than seeing the bottom of a barrel of ale. When the cold weather started approaching, we collected everything up and downed the lot!... Hic...
Shame you weren't here, we had a really good time! And by the time the ice monster showed up, we were already completely sloshed. Yeah... it was a good thing that the barrels were already empty. It meant we had somewhere to hide. A blessing in disguise, as the saying goes...
Anyway... we've been dealing with the enemy since early this morning. Does it show? We're stuck here, waiting for a new ship to arrive with supplies... hic! We're sure the others are still putting the ale away - yep, no doubt about it. Where's the justice in that, eh?
Listen... Could you pay a visit to the boss for us? We think he forgot to send someone to replace us. Hic... we'll be eternally in your debt. Just don't say anything to him about him being alone! It drives him absolutely mad.
I'm surprised to see that anyone out here is still sober...

Re-p-p-place who? Those old bellyaching fools must have lost their m-m-marbles. Replace them! They've only just gone on duty!
Last night they managed to down three b-b-bottles of ale and another two bottles of homebrew and completely d-d-drank themselves under the table. They're a disgrace! Let them sit out there and reflect on their behavior. I've had it up to here with their t-t-troubles.
Leave them there to suffer without anything to d-d-drink and without anyone to fuss over them. We G-G-Gibberlings are made of stern stuff!
Check on the patrols on the east and west sides on the allod.

The w-w-worst problem out here is the ice and the cold. We G-G-Gibberlings are a friendly, hard working people - even in these barren snowbound lands. But somehow an ice m-m-monster has found its way into these parts. We d-d-don't know anything about it except that it came from the Astral. I dispatched patrols to all f-f-four corners of the allod. But last night, in the middle of the drinking, the monster caught us unawares. I've no idea what happened to the p-p-patrols - they didn't light any flares or anything. Something's not r-r-right!
I can see you're up for an adventure. So, here's a challenge for you - head out to the eastern shore of the allod and f-f-find out what happened to the patrols that I posted there. After that, f-f-find the second patrol around Bold Hill.
Once you've found them... C-c-come back and see me.
Ah! Oh, my poor old heart. I almost jumped out of my skin...
So, the monster made it past the western p-p-patrol again... It's time we dealt with this p-p-problem by whatever means n-n-necessary...
Hug and help three frozen Gibberlings get warm. Report to the Attentive Family at the Quiet Harbor.

Do you see what that monster has done? These poor bastards didn't manage to hide in time. Just one blow of the monster's icy breath and that was it. Now we can't tell our Gibberling brothers apart from the icicles.
We don't know what to do. Maybe light a fire next to them? Or perhaps pour some boiling water over them? We don't want to upset them when they come round. No, we'll have to try a more tender approach - Gibberlings respond better to a gentle touch.
You'll have to hug each and every one of them as hard as possible and warm them up with your body heat. Just be careful that we don't end up having to defrost you too! Here, take some of this burning ale. Drink it as soon as you start to get cold. The ale might go to your head, but unfortunately that's unavoidable.
Make sure you don't only hug the females or the males - we won't judge. Just don't think of them as male or female, but merely as victims of the ice monster!
Just look at these poor, frozen specimens. They've turned blue from the cold!
Oh, thank you! Let us give you a hug!
Collect 4 Bundles of Curly Lichen for the Attentive Family in the Foothills of Arov.

Looks like I miscalculated and we ran out of ale... But then again, who could have anticipated how much we'd need to warm those guys up. Or maybe someone has been exaggerating how frozen they were and drank more than their fair share of the ale. Well, never mind, we can't do anything about it now.
To make ale, I need curly lichen. It grows in the Foothills of Arov, one of the neighboring allods. Go and fetch me four bundles of the curly lichen. You'll need some of the ale for yourself when you venture into the colder allods. Trust me.
Without curly lichen, there's no ale. And without ale, there's no Gibberlings!
Wow! I'd give you another hug if I thought you wouldn't take it the wrong way. But here's some ale for you troubles.
Go to Gray Lake, release a Blue Flare Rocket, kill 4 Snow Leopards, release a second Blue Flare Rocket, and return to Vicki the Red.

My brother Eric says there is no beast more dangerous than a bear. Do you know why? It's because yesterday he managed to kill one. Why would you do that? The poor bear barely got its paw out of its mouth. I feel for the beast. But leopards, leopards are a different story altogether. I don't even have the words to describe it. A leopard will be at you with its claws out before you can even spot it.
Anyway, I'm sure you can settle our dispute for us. Take these blue flare rockets. The snow leopards are near the Gray Lake. Fire a rocket when you spot the leopards, then kill 4 leopards, then fire the second rocket. Talk to Eric about the bears. We'll time how long it takes you to kill them from here. Whichever beasts take longer to kill are the most dangerous. It will be interesting to see who's right.
Don't forget to fire the blue flare rocket before you start hunting for the leopards.

That Eric is a jerk! As soon as I saw the blue flare I started my timer, but then he started distracting me with his stories. Now I don't even know who won! What a pity, it would have been an interesting wager...
Go to Bold Hill, release a Red Flare Rocket, kill 4 Polar Bears, release a second Red Flare Rocket, and return to Eric the Red.

Snow leopards are nothing but oversized pussycats. And no one's afraid of pussycats. But the bears - now those are real beasts! And believe me, I'd know. Vicki says leopards are more agile and quicker, which makes them more dangerous. That's feminine logic for you! Lice are even faster, but they're not exactly deadly, are they? No! What matters is the weight and bulk of the beast, how far they can reach when they swipe at you, and how big their teeth are. But she'll never learn...
Here's what we'll do. I'll give you two red flare rockets. You'll head out to Bold Hill, fire the first flare, kill four polar bears, and then fire the second flare as soon as you're finished. I'll time you. Talk to Vicki, she'll give you her rocket and tell you where the leopards are. Whichever takes the longest to kill is the more dangerous animal. It's pretty obvious to me. But let's show her, too!
Go and take care of the bears and the leopards, we'll time you and then we'll see that I was right.

Hmph! That's the fairer sex for you. As soon as you released the blue rocket she started prancing about and distracted me. I wasn't able to time you properly! Well, you've still done a good job - you've completely cleared the area of the beasts.
Kill 4 Snowbound Harpies for the Whispering Family.

Shhh! Keep your voice down! You'll scare the fish away! There's barely any as it is.
We've tried giving the lake harpies some fish to keep them happy, but now they're running amok. They attack fishermen and snatch fish right out of our hands. We're stuck out here freezing our rear ends off, while the others are in the village drinking away! All for nothing...
Please go and kill four harpies for us. That should stop them. I mean, every time we catch something, they're all over it within seconds.
I'm sure those harpies won't be doing any more fishing after that.

It looks like the harpies have become more cautious. They're circling the lake, but now they're afraid to get any closer. And we have you to thank for that! I'm afraid all I have to offer you is some fish. Here, take it.
Collect 2 Bark Beetles and 2 Fat Bark Beetles for the Whispering Family.

Shhh! We've dealt with the harpies, but now we have another problem. There's plenty of fish, but we've got nothing to catch it with. We're out of bait.
Why don't you take this fisherman's knife and fetch me some bark beetles from the trees. I need at least two... And the fatter, the better! Fish love the fat ones! At least two if you can find them. You'll be really helping us out.
The juicy bark beetles live on the trees in the forest. They make magnificent bait!
What would we have done without you? There'll be no Gibberlings dying of hunger now!
Check on the 3 markers around the allod for the Stout Family.

The ice monster attacked again? We had no idea. We haven't seen it. So it wasn't here. It's true. You don't believe us?
Okay, so our buddies may have brought us a couple bottles of homebrew, but we swear we didn't have any. We don't get drunk on that anyway. And not on guard duty, of course.
But we did notice something else...
the allod is getting bigger! Why are you looking at us like that?! Like we said, we don't get drunk on duty. But we're telling you, the Astral is retreating! You don't believe us? Fine...
We've placed eight markers around the edge of the allod. Go and have a look - you'll see for yourself that the Astral has shifted - if there's land beyond the markers, then you'll see we're telling the truth.
Pretty clever, right? We planted the markers at the edge of the allod. Now anyone who doesn't believe us can go and check for themselves!
Well? We were right, weren't we? What do you think this means? The territory that we're responsible for watching is expanding! That means we must be entitled to a pay raise!
Take the news to Froddy the Fidget in Quiet Harbor.

I don't think we'll be able to work out this mystery between the two of us. And especially not without any more homebrew to stimulate the brain cells... We'll need someone else to help us out here.
Go tell Froddy the Fidget, our High Druid. Musing on the mysteries of creation is what he does best.
There's good news and bad news. We're still waiting for the good news...
So, the allod is expanding... That's good! It's only bad when it gets smaller. But before we start celebrating we need to find out why it's happening.
Bring 4 pieces of Gritty Ore to the Stooping Family.

Tell us, has anyone seen a Great Mage's tower here? No? That's because there's none. And if there's no Great Mage around here, what does that mean? Well? Jeez, didn't they teach you anything about allod history in school?
If there's no Great Mage, that means there must be meteorite. It's elementary! If there's no meteorite, It means it simply hasn't been found yet. We'll have to go and find it!
In the yeti settlement on Bold Hill you'll find a cave with a ton of ore. We need seven samples of that ore. Here, we'll give you our hammer - take it and make your way into the lair of those hairy creatures. Now, don't think you can use the hammer on those monsters. It's a tool, not a weapon. Use the hammer to break off ore samples. Bring the samples to us. Are these instructions clear enough?
Is there something that we haven't made clear? We'll explain it again. This is a hammer. You use it to break off seven ore samples, got it? Then you return to us.
Well, you didn't do too badly. Your contribution to science will not go unnoticed. We definitely won't forget what you've done... especially if this ore sample contains any traces of meteorite.
Look for Atli the Colossal in the Foothills of Arov.

What's the story with the "Sparrow"? Is everyone alive? It was us who let the monster slip through the net... but it wasn't our fault!
We were attacked by savages from the neighboring allod. They're mountainfolk, they call themselves the Ar. There were tons of them, a higher number than I could count, so we had to switch to Plan B - we scattered.
That's when the monster showed up. If you want to know why I didn't light the fire, it's because I was too busy hiding behind that hill over yonder and the savages were by the fire, so how could I have lit it?
When the savages left, I noticed that Atli and Barni were missing and I have no idea where they are. I'm really afraid for them! But I can't leave my post to go look for them - so could I bother you to go to the Ar camp? Maybe the savages have taken them and have them there. Okay?
Oh my, it looks like I'm not going to die after all!
Hey, I'm Atli. Please say that you're looking for me.
Collect 4 pieces of Bear Meat and place them in the chest in the Foothills of Arov. Report back to the Stubborn Family in Quiet Harbor.

What are we doing here? Who can we trade with? We need some big deals! What are we supposed to do here? Sell beads to the yetis?
There's a mountain tribe on that allod over there, but all those savages know how to do is fight. Trading with them is a little strange - we leave our goods out for them in an agreed location, and the next day we go back and collect whatever they give in exchange.
It's mainly just skins, claws, and innards - that's all they ever have that's worth taking. We know it's not much, but you've got to start somewhere. We're like missionaries, bringing the light of civilization to this backward people.
Truth be told, we're doing this all at a loss - it's all about the principle. Often times, we'll leave our goods there for them and get zilch in return! But we're not ones to give up that easily! We've decided to give it one more go. So, do you want to help us bring civilization to these savages?

We'd like to point out that while it may be the mages who maintain the allods it's us, the traders, who unite the whole world. We might go broke, but we're forcing those barbarians to trade with us! That's how civilization is born!

So, how are you liking your role as a missionary? What's that?! An ambush by the savages?! It looks like not all of those savages are ready for mutually beneficial cooperation. It seems like our friendly relationship has come to an end. Looks like it's time for us to find a new pursuit.
Kill 4 Arctic Yetis and report back to the Cunning Family.

Sure, it's cold in these parts, but we're just glad to have firm ground under our feet. And just look at how clean the air is! And there are fish in the lake - okay, not many, but still... Really, this place isn't as bad as people say.
However, we're not without danger. Not far from Quiet Harbor, just up in the hills, is a group of yetis. We have no idea just how intelligent they might be. We've tried to make contact with them but it's only caused them to attack our harbor. They're frightening, bloodthirsty creatures...
As captains we're responsible for the safety of the crew even when we're on land. Maybe you can help. Please go kill ten yetis for us. We must show them that there are consequences for every action! Then they'll stop attacking our camp.
Bloodshed is always a terrible thing, but there's no other alternative in this case.
It's a shame that the yetis didn't understand us. Maybe they really don't have anything going on inside those heads of theirs.
Go to the altar in the Foothills of Arov and find Barni the Courageous.
I'm fine, but Barni is in trouble! Those savages have taken him to the altar. They want to sacrifice him to some kind of "Ice God." I beg of you, please be swift! Go save him!

Hm... You know, this isn't the first time that I've died. I made it out of Purgatory before, thank Tensess, but this time I'm getting a different kind of vibe. It feels as if I'm being pulled away... Far away... Maybe because I was used as a sacrifice.
Hm, definitely not my idea of fun. The good news is that I sense a kind of levity in my whole body and I don't feel cold anymore! Well, enough about that... I don't have long until I'm pulled away for good, so listen up and let's make this quick.
Maybe if I summon the Gibberling Ghost, I'll find out what happened here?
Tell Torn the Stutterer about the dragon.

The ice monster isn't from the Astral, it lives here, on the archipelago. What's more, our monster, this so-called "Ice God" of the savages, is one in the same! One creature with two faces... If you can call that a face! Well, whatever you want to call it, it's still there...
It looks like a dragon. So, be sure to inform Torn as well.
Say hi to Atli and Ella for me if you get the chance. They'll probably have a tough time without me. But then again, the two Reds are doing okay on their own and Torn and Froddy have been left with no family at all. We Gibberlings are a tough breed, I'm sure they'll manage. That's about it, I can't stay here any longer. Farewell...
Oh, what should I d-d-do? I've been torturing myself with this question for days now. What if these m-m-monster attacks continue and our shipments keep getting delayed?
The ice monster is a d-d-dragon? It gets worse by the hour!
Bring the Curly Family 4 Harpy Wings from the Foothills of Arov or Gray Lake.

Oh... My head feels like it's going to explode... All three of them. Can you imagine that?!
I don't know if it's because I spent all day yesterday working away with a hammer or because I spent all night drinking. What do you think? Yes, must be the hammer.
What does it mean when a boat is moored? You need to mend this or that... What a headache! It's endless. I'm dying here and you want to know about the sails? They've been worn completely thin and our spare sail was shred to ribbons in the last storm. And we've used up all our cloth! Hmm... Maybe Inga would be willing to take something off... Now there's a thought! Unfortunately, it wouldn't be enough for our needs.
We've heard there are harpies on the allod. If only we could make use of their wide, leathery wings...
Hey, it might actually work! I'd say we need two of those wings... no, two wouldn't be enough. Four would do it! Will you help us?
How would someone manage without sails? Do they pull the ships with a rope or something? They don't have haulers out in the Astral, do they?
Much obliged! Now we just need to fix up the sail for the Astral by tomorrow at the latest!
Collect 1 Underripe Fir Seed, 1 Ripe Fir Seed, and 1 Overripe Fir Seed for Froddy the Fidget.

I've been doing a lot of thinking and maybe it's for the best that there's no hope of reclaiming our homeland - enough of all this venturing off into the Astral! The time has come to face the facts and realize that this is our home now!
Yes, this archipelago will be our new home. I'm sure that the rest of the Gibberlings will agree with me and we'll organize a magnificent feast in honor of our new home.
However, it's not the right time to reveal the truth to my people. We already have enough problems and no one likes the taste of tears in their beer.
Fortunately, I'm a druid! How hard can it really be to transform this icy land into a flourishing garden?! There are beautiful and giant fir trees growing on Shaggy Isle and it's colder there than it is here. I want to find out how they can survive there.
Go fetch me some of their seeds. Please make sure that they're varying levels of ripeness. It'll greatly speed up my research if they are.
Fir trees have cones, and inside the cones there are seeds, and in those seeds there is a forest.
I'm eternally grateful to you. I can sense that these seeds contain some sort of mysterious power. I'll need to examine them very carefully.
Bring the Rosycheeked Family 4 Owl Eggs.

Phew... We've just now finished washing the remaining dishes. Our men have broken so many pots and mugs this time! First they started clinking their mugs so hard they kept breaking the handles! Then that monster attacked and nobody cared to watch where they were going! How's that for a "bottoms up!"
We need to start scrubbing these tables. In the meantime, I need you to bring me four eggs of arctic owls. They live on Shaggy Isle. Naturally, they won't be happy to see you poking around in their nests. But we have an idea... We're going to tame the tiny, fluffy baby owls from those eggs. Don't look so surprised! Just look at the Kanians, they use owls to carry the mail all the time. Then we can breed enough to supply us with meat and eggs too! Now that's what we call progress!
We tamed a rhinocerous once, so owls should be a piece of cake.
Thank you! Now we just have to figure out who's going to hatch these eggs...
Bring 2 Black Ore Samples and 2 Red Ore Samples to the Stooping Family.

There are no signs of meteorite in this rock. So, what does this mean? It's elementary! This can only mean that the meteorite is somewhere else.
There's a cave on Shaggy Isle that is inhabited by monsters. The monsters are very interesting from a biological viewpoint. They're werebears and they're incredibly ferocious and cruel. Luckily, one of our scouts managed to make it out alive. He told us there's an abundance of both black and red ore in the cave! We are itching to study it!
You understand what needs to be done, right? Take the hammer and get to work. We're going to need four ore samples from the cave: two black and two red.
Our research has hit a dead end, but this is just a temporary setback, we're sure of it...
We're on the right track! Alright, enough chatter, we need to examine the ore.
Kill 4 Frosty Werebears and report back to the Clever Family.

The yetis have quieted down thanks to you. Unfortunately, there's still one more unpleasant task to complete. This time our conscience will be clear when we send you to slaughter these beasts. I'm sending you after the Werebears. They have the worst features of animals and humans! These creatures must be exterminated!
Go in and kill twelve Werebears in their cave on Shaggy Isle.
Werebears... nature can create the most revolting creatures!
Thank you! Shaggy Isle will now be a much safer place.
Get the Silver Fur from the Sangiyok and bring it to Vicki the Red.

Listen, there are strange things developing on Shaggy Isle. I've set several snow leopard traps over there and when I check on them, I see that they've all gone off but not a single animal has been caught. It seems that the only thing I've been able to catch is a clump of silvery fur.
I'm afraid that there's an unusually intelligent and crafty snow leopard in the woods. I'm only bringing this up because I figure that maybe you'd enjoy the challenge in hunting this cunning beast. Let's see who can track him down faster, you or I. Our proof will be the skin with silver fur.
I still can't track down that crafty silver snow leopard... maybe you'll have better luck.
Wow, you are really something else! You're as good a hunter as I am! My hat's off to you!
Retrieve an Astral Battery for the Curly Family.

No, I haven't started on the sails yet. It still feels like someone put a pot on my head and gave it a good whack.
And now it looks like I've made a huge blunder. Please, I beg of you, just don't tell Inga. I threw our Astral batteries into the Astral to... well, to charge them up a bit. But then a storm kicked up the next thing I know is that the batteries are gone and so is the mead!
Judging by the wind direction, I'd say that the batteries must have been blown off to the northeast, probably somewhere around Cold Isle. But on the other hand, this was a serious storm, so they could have scattered across all the neighboring allods.
Could you jump over there and see if you can find one? We lost five regular batteries and five modernized big ones, but we only need one. Please, there's no one else I can ask.
If you're here, then that means that the ship batteries are drifting somewhere around Cold Isle...
You found one! Oh, my darling battery! I could just kiss them. Oh, thank you! I'm in your debt for as long as I live!
Bring the head of the Great Polar Bear to Eric the Red.

I was sailing past the Ugrov Ridge the other day and noticed a polar bear thi-i-is big! You just wouldn't believe how big it was! I wish I could get my hands on its head to hang on the wall in my cabin. That's if it fits through the door, of course. Well, if worse comes to worst, we could tear down the bulkhead.
But I don't have the time to hunt it, I need to get meat for our men and the ship. So, if you're up to the challenge and not scared - then the bear is yours. But the head, naturally, is mine. I did see it first, after all!
What, are you chicken? Afraid to take on some polar bear? Hmph. That's what I thought.

You managed to take it down?
I'm speechless! You have my respect!
Find out how the savages from Ugrov Ridge summon the icy dragon.

We've never run into a d-d-dragon before, but there's nothing that G-G-Gibberlings can't handle when they use their heads. Let's try to trick the m-m-monster.
There is another mountain p-p-people living on the ridge, the Urg Tribe - I'm sure that they also worship the ice monster. I know that this is very dangerous, but you need to s-s-sneak into their camp and find out how they summon the d-d-dragon, maybe we can also lure it into coming to us.
Oh yeah, it's very c-c-cold on Ugrov Ridge, so make sure you bring a supply of burning ale with you or you might risk getting f-f-frostbite on your n-n-nose.
Poor, wretched Tooh the Rotten! He was torn out of his people's jaw and thrown out into the street!

The Arg threw poor old Tooh the Rotten out. Tooh the Rotten was the one who kept bringing skins, claws, and entrails to the place where meat appears. Tooh the Rotten wants to live on friendly terms with those weird goblins from the big boat. But Arg don't want that, they chased Tooh the Rotten away and set up an ambush near the place where the meat appears. The Urgs also chased Tooh the Rotten away. They want to kill the weird goblins from the big boat as a gift to their ice god. What does this goblin want with them? Ask Tooh the Rotten.
Take the Blood Colored Artifact from Kewell the Heartripper and take it to Torn the Stutterer.

This mountainfolk is looking for the ice god? The ice god feels the scent of scarlet life and then he comes. When there's no stranger to take lots of scarlet life from, Krewell the Heartripper picks up the Great Red Treasure and takes his own scarlet life and the soul of the ice, then the ice god hears the call and comes.
The Urg Tribe had the Great Red Treasure even before my grandfather's grandfather left his mother's womb. They say the Urg Tribe and the Arg Tribe became enemies after the ice god came.
Take the Great Red Treasure away from Krewell if you want to talk to the god. But remember that the ice god brings evil - Tooh warned you!
How did you do? Manage to l-l-learn anything?

What is this? L-l-looks like some old June knick-knack. Is this really what the Urg Tribe uses to summon their "ice god?" Hm... Maybe we should show this thing to Froddy?
... Actually, this can wait. There's more important b-b-business to attend to. While you were gone, we had another m-m-misfortune.
Collect 4 chunks of Frozen Meat for the Custard Family in the Quiet Harbor.

No! We told you, there's no more mead! There's nothing at all - we don't even have meat or fish!
Instead of hanging around the harbor, why don't you go do something useful? Our scouts saw some yaks frozen into blocks of ice on Ugrov Ridge. This is a wonderful opportunity to prove your valor and supply the ship with meat at the same time. Take this ice pick. Fight your way through the hordes of hungry polar bears and chop up four chunks of frozen meat for us. Any hero that accomplishes this task will have an additional daily pint of mead coming to them.
Frozen yaks were found embedded in the ice. It's like nature prepared a meat locker for us Gibberlings.
A hero! Our great hero! We mean that. But as to that daily pint of mead... Uh... Alas... It seems we overestimated our stocks...
Collect 3 Ice Elements for the Torn the Stutterer.

That d-d-dragon visited us again. We need to do something. But now we have the J-J-June artifact. We can summon the dragon like those m-m-mountain people do and when it appears, we'll attack and f-f-finish it off! But we have one problem though...
As the savage said, the ritual requires "scarlet life" which has to be b-b-blood, that's a no-brainer. And we also need the "soul of the ice."
Froddy, the Cunning Family, and the Stooping Family all agree that this "s-s-soul of the ice..." Um... How do I put it... It's the substance of the ice, the essence of elementals and is f-f-found somewhere deep within them.
I'm not a scientist, so this explanation must sound c-c-confusing... You will have to go to the Cold or Nordheim Isles and tear the ice s-s-soul out of some ice elemental. I would rec-c-commend Cold Isle... It's c-c-colder there, but not as dangerous... It'll be hard, so get r-r-ready!
T-t-to be honest, I'm n-n-not comfortable with these shamanic rituals... But we need to take care of this dragon or he'll never leave us in p-p-peace here.
I am so happy to see you! You're coming to our aid again! Alright, w-w-wait, we'll get everything ready for the ritual.
Kill 4 Icy Trolls on the Cold Isle and report back to the Captains of the Little Sparrow.

You probably think I'm some cold hearted battle axe. That I don't care about anything as long as I get to kill someone. That's not true. The captain's position entails responsibility. And sometimes it's better to be overly vigilant than let your crew be killed.
So I'm sending you out to Cold Isle where some very scary creatures live - trolls. Striking first will be the right thing to do.
Go kill four trolls and the Gibberlings will sleep a little better at night.
Trolls... We used to think there was nothing worse than mosquitoes.
Wonderful! The trolls are dead and I can finally stop to take a breath - we won't have to worry about an attack from this side.
Set 4 Buoys on Cold Isle and report back to the Curly Family.

You're not going to believe this, but I've just had a great idea! I'm not sure how I managed, but it did!
All of our ship's troubles are due to the fact that there aren't any proper navigational directions in Frozen Frontier! No one has bothered to set up any buoys! Oh, those are usually a signal beacon or a signaler with flags on the coast. Given the conditions, it's no surprise that ships are crashing on the rocks... But we can change that!
Go to Cold Isle and put up signal beacons along the coast. If you do this, the captains will be able to navigate between these allods on our way home without worrying about damaging the ship.
I can probably ask for a bonus for my innovative proposal with the beacons!
Are the beacons set? Great! I'm going to comb my hair and go tell the captain about your heroism. Well... our heroism...
Speak with Froddy the Fidget in Quiet Harbor.

Hm, no signs of meteorite again! What could this mean? No, it doesn't mean we'll send you out to get more samples. However, the ore from the werebears' cave poses a conundrum. It seems like the stone had been melted from a very powerful fire. It also seems to be imbued with magical power of some sort.
What should we do? Well, that's obvious! We need to inform Froddy the Fidget, our elder. Magic is his forte, you know. He should be able to tell us what these strange signs mean.
It's like a test for me every time you come around. I have to guess what sort of unbelievable news you've brought me!
There's magical power in the ore? I wonder if it's similar to the power that I sensed in the Great Tree's seeds... Give me some time to think about all of this...
Deliver the Crate of Burning Ale to the Burly Family.

You know, I believe these seeds posses a magical power that helps the trees grow in these harsh conditions. It looks like this ore contains a similar power. I have a feeling that we're getting closer to uncovering this archipelago's secret.
There's a tribe of trolls that live on Cold Isle and they're another link in this mysterious chain. Living beings! How do they survive there and why haven't they frozen to death?
We sent a group of brave explorers to Cold Isle headed by the Burly Family, but we haven't heard a thing from them since. Please find them and take them a box of ale - it's very useful for dealing with the cold weather.
Well now, we must be seeing ghosts. We've gone and drank far too much!
We don't believe our eyes! You're breathing! You look well and don't seem to have frostbite! How did you manage to get here?
Purchase Burning Ale from the Attentive Family.

You're going to Cold Isle? You better remember, it's real easy to croak in that place. Don't even think about setting foot out there without some burning ale. It'll warm you right up when you start to get frostbitten!
Make sure you drop by and see the Attentive Family before you leave. They keep a bunch of ale around at all times. You'll thank us later!
What? Do you want a hug?

A trip to Cold Isle without Burning Ale is not just dumb, it's criminally insane!
Here, take this.
Destroy 4 Frosty Demon Scouts and return to the Burly Family.

Thank you for the ale. But unfortunately, many of our boys have died, so we don't need this much...
You wouldn't believe what happened here. Things were quiet at first - we dug into the snow and watched the trolls. That's no easy task! They stand still for hours on end and you don't know whether they're asleep or lost in thought... But then demons came out of the Astral! What could have made them leave their element? No idea.
Our boys fought bravely and we're proud of them. Killed nearly all the demons.
Four demons still remain on the shore - their scouts. Disgusting little creatures.
Could you deal with them?
The only language you'll find that they understand is the language of death!
We're saved! You've given us hope! Now we can start studying this allod again!
Discover the secret of the trolls' ruins and return to the Burly Family.

Let's get back to our main objective. We've encountered trolls several times, killed a few, and even had to eat one. The meat was a bit tough, but not much tougher than a horse's.
What? A real Gibberling doesn't seek comfort - instead they try to reach places where no one has set foot before. Sometimes that comes at a high price... Anyway, we still don't know how the trolls survive in this terrible climate.
Then again, their survival may be in danger at the moment due to the appearance of the ice elementals. They've driven the trolls out by capturing the ruins where they used to live. We suspect there won't be any trolls left soon - they'll all die out like the yaks did on Ugrov Ridge.
We must investigate those ruins! It's clear to us that the trolls didn't have any problem with the cold until their ruins were captured by the elementals. We were planning a trip there, but the demons put a stop to that, so we're forced to ask you to do this for us.
A strange artifact appears to have been placed here...
A strange artifact appears to have been placed here...
Take the Ice Colored Artifact to Froddy the Fidget.

What a strange artifact... It's a frozen teardrop that emits waves of heat. This must explain how the trolls are able to survive here. However, as soon as the artifact is removed from the pedestal it becomes as cold as ice.
This should be taken to Froddy the Fidget as soon as possible! It be uncover the secret behind the archipelago's strange magic!
What is it this time? Another important discovery?
Oh, dear! My head is spinning! This artifact is as cold as the land itself! You probably won't be surprised to hear me say that I need to think things over!
Summon the Ice King by using the artifact, your blood, and an Ice Element. Participate in killing it and report to Torn the Stutterer.

Everything's r-r-ready for the r-r-ritual! Remember what the savage told you - you need to use the artifact, your blood, and the "s-s-soul of ice."
I fear that the dragon is too powerful but I have come up with a way of defeating him! See those Astral c-c-cannons? Try to wound him while he's in the air and then finish him off on the ground. Kill the monster and the G-G-Gibberlings will reward you handsomely! Good luck!
Sometimes when I am deep in thought I don't notice anything around me... What's going on?

So, the dragon is dead. Are you s-s-surprised that I know? I don't want to scare you but it looks like the dragon wasn't the worst of it. That June artifact has b-b-begun to speak!
Someone has been communicating with me via the artifact and whoever they are they're very unhappy with what we did to the d-d-dragon, their accomplice.
I have a fairly good idea who it is, but maybe you ought to sit down before I tell you! There's a Great D-D-Dragon on our archipelago! That explains everything - the lava, the power within the s-s-seeds, the lack of meteorite, the r-r-receding Astral and even the appearance of the demons.
The demons have been enemies with d-d-dragons since the beginning of time, you! It makes sense that they'd attack them! Now what do you think of that?
While you're thinking it over, take a l-l-look at these weapons. Take whichever you fancy - it's your reward for killing the ice m-m-monster.
Find the Great Dragon on Nordheim Isle.

As you may know, there's an Orcish allod that's supported by a Great Dragon instead of a Great Mage. I believe this may be true of our archipelago as well. The only difference is that our local dragon has been weakened by something. That means we must seize this opportunity!
If we offer him help then maybe he'll let us stay here. Our lives hang by a thread - it's time that we stand or fall. I believe that the dragon can only be in one part of the archipelago - Nordheim Isle, the most remote allod of them all.
The allod reeks of death! We've never ventured that far but the time for heroism has come. You must find the dragon and try to come to some sort of understanding with him. This mission is a great honor and an even greater test of your courage!
There's no dragon... But there is a strange shining creature that looks like a huge will-o'-the-wisp. As soon as you get near it, a terrible chill comes over your heart!
Speak with the Captain of the Little Sparrow.

I know I've made you w-w-wander the whole archipelago but I have one l-l-last request. Oh, don't make that face at me. Go tell our wonderful c-c-captain that we have cannonballs. Got it? Tell her word for word - "We've got cannonballs!"
I've been waiting for you, the first mate let me know that you were coming...
Hm, cannonballs made from cave gargoyle hearts. Yeah, this will do just fine, like last time! You'll see soon enough, just don't go too far.
Speak with the Captain of the Little Sparrow.

You have great potential to be an explorer! It's easy, isn't it?
It's all because of that potential. If you read, think, compare, and analyze everything, we'll be colleagues in no time. But for now, I have the easiest and final mission from the Stooping Family. Go and tell Inga that I was right and that it's lapis lazuli. Tell her what I said word for word "it's lapis lazuli!" Make sure you get it right!
Finally. The Stooping Family kept promising me that you'd come...
Oh, lapis lazuli! It's the most wonderful thing I've ever seen on this allod. You'll see what I mean soon enough.

Wait a second! Look, the seal is broken! See that crack? I guess it could've been me, with the way I swung my arms around. Or maybe you, on your trip back... So, does that mean that the dragon resurrected already?! Oops.
Let me try to get in touch with him now... Uh oh! Our dead friend is very angry... His soul has returned to his body, but he can't get out. The rock and ice surround his body. He's completely trapped!
...Oh, my. What an interesting word! A real ancient one! It seems that our dragon needs our help once again! We'll have to melt through the ice and help the dragon break free. I know exactly how we can do that, they don't call me a wise man for nothing!
There's a Great Tree that grows in Darkwater. It's tended to by Kanian druids. The power of Great Trees can melt the ice and warm up the frozen earth. Perhaps they'll share some of their seeds with us. We could plant a Great Tree here, grow it big and strong, and it will melt the ground so the dragon could break free!
Listen, I'm sorry for troubling you again... But maybe you could find some time to go to Darkwater and ask them for a seed? We don't have anyone else that we can count on...
I suppose that now is as a good a time as any to address the nation. What do you think sounds better - "my fellow Gibberlings, we no longer have a home" or "my fellow Gibberlings, we have found a home?" Yes, I guess I like the second option too.
The Great Tree! Long have I dreamt of resting under its branches!

The seeds of the Great Tree... Hm, I don't think it's going to be that easy. Things are very difficult in Darkwater at the moment. The Valir castle has been cursed and nobody's been able to set foot inside it for twenty years. The natural equilibrium has been disturbed and darkness is amassing in the forests. Would the Great Tree be willing to share its power? It's hard to say.
Fire the Little Sparrow's cannons using the Special Fuse. Report to the Cunning Family.

You want to know how Gibberlings will take the news that they've lost their home? We've all known for a long time. I overheard your first conversation with Froddy and didn't feel the need to keep it quiet from the Gibberlings.
The Little Sparrow has been our refuge for years and we'll make a real home out of it now! The Gibberlings have readied their barrels of beer - but the supply ship never came, I wonder where all this beer came from? They've probably been saving it.
And we have a surprise for you. The lapis lazuli and the gargoyle hearts that you spent so much effort procuring are not strategic weapons, they're... Well, you'll see. Take this special fuse and fire the cannons!
What? You don't want to fire the cannons? I don't believe it!
Remember, you've got friends here! Come back and you'll always receive a warm welcome, a hearty meal, and more than enough brew to wash it down with! Hah!
Take some ale to the Snoring Family.

It's a good day and we've g-g-got many things to celebrate! We killed the ice monster, came to an agreement with the Great D-D-Dragon, and found a new home... That calls for a party! Hic!
A drinks r-r-reception will be announced soon -"Bottoms Up: Part Two." Everyone is welcome! We were even going to invite the d-d-dragon but thought that he probably wouldn't enjoy it. And we've got plenty of folks here who'll down a b-b-barrel of ale in seconds.
Oh, no! We forgot about the Snoring Family! They're probably still at their post! Cold! And sober! That just won't do. Go take them a bottle of ale so that they can have a good time too.

This is for us?! Oh, what a wonderful day - you're the third person to bring us a bottle!
Who's this one from? Torn?! Wow!
He's good man, you know, but totally nutty in the head. Didn't you know? He lost all his brothers! Some Astral tore them to shreds, so resurrection is out of the question... He was the only survivor and he has stuttered ever since. But he doesn't believe that his brothers are dead - he thinks they just moved to some other ship. I guess that's the only way he can live on.
But hey, that's not something that we should be thinking about, right? Let's drink one in honor of their memory! Theirs and all the others who are not here with us to see this great day!
Obtain 4 Stone Hearts of Cave Gargoyles on Nordheim Isle for Torn the Stutterer.

Damn, as soon as we deal with one p-p-problem there's another one waiting to take its place. They just keep building up.
You're going to Nordheim? Well, given that you're putting your body on the l-l-line we might as well get as much use out of it that we can. I have a job for you. You will meet, and undoubtedly defeat, some t-t-terrible monsters called cave gargoyles.
Please take their hearts for me. The hearts are made of stone and make great cannonballs. Surprised? Don't be, it's true! The best cannonballs a G-G-Gibberling can get, I swear on the memory of our lost home!
A few years ago we landed on an allod with cave gargoyles. That's where we found that their stone hearts made for amazing cannonballs!
Great! It's w-w-wonderful to feel the weight of these heavy hearts in my hands once again.
Collect 4 chunks of Lapis Lazuli on Nordheim Isle for the Stooping Family.

It seems that some corrections must be made to our initial calculations - there is no Great Mage, there is no meteorite... But there is something better than a Great Mage and a meteorite put together - a Great Dragon! You could say that the results exceeded our expectations.
Now, listen carefully for I do not like to repeat myself or waste my time. Our scouts have reported that a rare mineral, lapis lazuli, can be found on Nordheim.
There won't be any mistakes this time - I was able to recognize it from the description. It's a very useful material, I swear. We need it badly, so do everything you can to get me some of that lapis lazuli.
I can't be wrong this time! The lapis lazuli was spotted on Nordheim.
I told you it was lapis lazuli! See? All I needed to reach the correct conclusion was a brief description made by a simple scout. I have to say that I couldn't have managed without you. Good job!
Continue the conversation with the Dragon's Soul.

The cold penetrates deeper and deeper, and a strange hissing voice is heard in the frozen cave.
"A warm blooded creature... A child of the world... It's been a long, long time since I saw one of your kind... It was not a pleasant meeting... Sit, child, and I will tell you all about it.
It was a brutal and bloody war. A great tribe of people, if the word "great" could ever be used in reference to those June, attacked us dragons. Many fell... Including myself.
Pestilent Wolf! That was the name of the Great June Mage that slew our dragons mercilessly. He led me into a deceitful trap. It was there when I found out that he was skilled not only in the power of ice, but also in blood magic.
You are fortunate that it no longer exists in this world. He bound me with eternal cold and sealed it with three blood seals and I could do nothing to resist him...
My body, my beautiful, strong body is buried deep inside this mountain, still bound by the power of his magic. But my spirit is not dead... I can return to life!
Though, I don't understand why. Something has happened in this accursed world while I was dead...
Oh, sorry. Heh, it seems my strength is coming back! I'll loosen my grip now before you also die. Then we can continue our conversation..."
The chilling cold subsides and you can breathe again.

I'll tell you what I've learned! My spirit, or soul as you call it in your mind, has returned to my grave. I feel I can spring back to life! Spread my wings... and fly again! But my body is still enchained by the June magic. By these three seals...
The savages were the first to break a seal. They fed it blood and that gave me strength. I could raise my head and summon my dragon servants.
The second seal was found by trolls. They used the ancient magic to stay warm, but it was broken when the seal left its altar. It is not gone for good.
The third seal is all that remains. It's well-hidden and protected by ancient curses. You will break it so that I can be released!
Wait until the dragon finishes his conversation with the Froddy the Fidget.

I have spoken. Now a decision must be made - help me and become my allies or turn into my new enemies. Both outcomes seem equally interesting... Relax, I know very well that it's not for you to decide.
Please wait while I talk to your forest mage. It seems that he's much more aware of how the world has changed over the last several thousand years. But, of course, even he doesn't know everything.
I will go speak with him now - I have many questions for him. Please just wait here.
Didn't I ask you to wait?

Your forest mage and I have come to an agreement. You will carry out your purpose and break the third, main seal, and I shall help your people settle on this snowy land and take you under my wing.
Now, you must do exactly what I say.
Destroy the Ancient June Golem, acquire the Third Seal, and take it to the Froddy the Fidget.

"There's an enchanted June golem, which stands deep inside the cave. He guards the final seal. One of my dragons was supposed to finish him off, but try as I did, I just couldn't subdue his will to mine. The dumb beast forgot who his master was!
You will take his place and kill the golem. He is powerful, and you will need my help, so I will share my power with you. Once you retrieve the seal, take it to your leader. He'll know what to do with it. Good bye, child of this accursed world!"
Be quiet, you don't have to say anything! It's surprising, but it's one of those rare cases when I already know everything myself!

Communicating with an ancient creature like a dragon, even a dead one, clears your head right up... Just think about it - he's been here for thousands of years, before the Great Cataclysm! Hell, even before the June people perished! I wonder where his soul has been all this time?!
There's a lot to think about here. This must be a gift from Tensess - nothing else could explain the dragon coming back to life! Of course, it probably helped that his body was completely preserved, protected by the June magic and the ice... like the embalmed bodies of the Zem people.
So, let's see that third seal... So, if I break it it'll release the dragon? That's a little creepy. Before I do this, please accept this humble gift from my people. It's much less than you deserve, but it's the dearest thing we can give you as a token of our appreciation.
